body:
NO-ACCESS-FIRST DDOS READINESS VALIDATION

Prove DDoS readiness without handing over your cloud keys.

No-access-first DDoS readiness validation for customer-declared targets.

Request access
See how validation works

What every verdict carries

target_id
A customer-declared FQDN, DNS zone, or TCP surface
confidence
external_only
verdict
protected

bypassable
inconclusive

References to the probe evidence behind the verdict
reason_codes
Why correlation reached this verdict
Field names from the verdict record. Values show what each field holds, not a customer result.
From declared target to readiness verdict.

A verdict is the end of a chain you can inspect, not a substitute for it. Each step records what the next one is allowed to rely on.

01
Declare the targets

List the FQDNs, DNS zones, and TCP surfaces in scope, by hand or through CSV or API import, and group them with tags. Ownership is proven, for example with a DNS TXT challenge, before any probe runs.

Recorded as
target
tags
ownership_status

02
Probe from the outside

Signed, rate-bounded probe jobs observe each approved target from outside your network. There is no agent to install and no cloud credential to grant.

Recorded as
check_id
probe_result

03
Keep the evidence

Each observation is stored with the check and the expected behavior it was tested against. A missing observation stays a visible gap. It is never filled in by inference.

Recorded as
evidence_ids
expected_behavior

04
Reach a readiness verdict

Correlation turns evidence into a verdict such as protected, exposed, bypassable, or inconclusive, with the reason codes behind it. Exports carry custody metadata for review and audit.

Recorded as
verdict
reason_codes
confidence

Separate lane, SOC only

Escalate through the SOC

High-scale tests are requested, never self-served. The SOC reviews authorization, schedules the window, runs the test, and holds the stop control.

Recorded as
high_scale_request_id

What it requires, and what it refuses to assume.

Four limits shape every validation run, from the first declared target to a SOC-run high-scale test.

Scope
Customer-declared targets.

You choose the exact FQDNs, DNS zones, and TCP surfaces in scope. AstraNull does not perform automatic IP inventory discovery.

Access
No infrastructure keys by default.

The no-access-first path needs no customer cloud credentials and no installed agent. Validation runs from the outside in.

Execution
Bounded checks behind an ownership gate.

Safe checks run as bounded probe jobs, and only against targets with proven ownership. Missing evidence stays visible instead of being inferred.

Escalation
High-scale stays governed.

Customers request high-scale work. The SOC validates authorization, schedules execution, and keeps the stop controls and the audit trail.

Default validation is bounded and defensive. AstraNull does not expose self-service attack tooling or unmanaged traffic generation.

High-scale testing is a SOC decision, not a button.

Customers can ask for a high-scale test. Only the AstraNull SOC can approve, schedule, execute, stop, and close one.

Customer

Request

Name the declared target group, the objective, a preferred window, and reachable contacts.

AstraNull SOC

Review, run, and close
Scope review
Authorization review
Risk review
Schedule
Go or no-go
Execute
Monitor
Stop or complete
Report

A kill switch must be available before start. Production tests need SOC analyst and SOC lead approval, scope locks after final approval, and every decision lands in the audit log.

Compare the operating model, not a marketing score.

The difference is where scope comes from, what access is required, who controls high-scale work, and what evidence remains after the run.
